parts.t: Neighbourhood guide · Fraser Valley Regional District Electoral Area C, tagged Mission in MLS® · Sasquatch Mountain Resort, FVRD Area C
Hemlock is an MLS® sub-area name. The Fraser Valley Regional District doesn’t publish a boundary for it. Hemlock Valley is in the Fraser Valley Regional District, not the City of Mission.
The plan says the largest town nearby is Agassiz, approximately 38 km from Hemlock Valley, and that Mission is approximately 55 km west.

The FVRD’s Hemlock Valley Official Community Plan covers the entire Controlled Recreation Area that the Province established in 2016 when it approved the Hemlock Valley All Seasons Resort Master Plan, for what is now Sasquatch Mountain Resort.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 18, 2026. I have worked in Lower Mainland real estate since 2015. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the Fraser Valley Regional District and Mission Public Schools (School District 75).
General information only.
Not legal, planning or financial advice. Confirm zoning, plan designations, flood rules and school catchments before you buy or sell.

Planning, zoning and flood

blocks.text: Planning and flood notes for Hemlock Valley

parts.t: Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.

The FVRD’s Hemlock Valley Official Community Plan covers the entire Controlled Recreation Area that the Province established in 2016 when it approved the Hemlock Valley All Seasons Resort Master Plan, for what is now Sasquatch Mountain Resort.
The FVRD Board adopted the Hemlock Valley Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 1626, 2021) on March 17, 2022.
The plan divides the area into three Neighbourhood Planning Areas: Hemlock West, Hemlock East and Hemlock North.

The plan’s land use designations are Village Planning Area, Managed Recreation, Open Recreation and Natural / Protected. Residential and industrial development is generally prohibited in the Managed Recreation and Open Recreation designations.
The plan says access is from Harrison Mills by a 12-mile road that began as a private logging road (now Hemlock Valley Road) and was gazetted by the Ministry of Transportation and Infrastructure.
The plan’s hazard chapter names snow avalanche, flooding, landslide, debris flows, river erosion and wildfire interface risk.

Development Permit Area 2-HW, the Mount Keenan Snow Avalanche Hazard Development Permit Area, applies to residential areas at the base of Mount Keenan, based on an October 2020 avalanche hazard assessment that studied residential parcels along Edelweiss Drive.

The plan’s zones are White (low hazard, avalanche return period greater than 1:300 years, where occupied structures are normally permitted), Blue (moderate hazard, 1:30 to 1:300 years, where occupied structures may be permitted with conditions) and Red (high hazard, 1:30 years, where occupied structures should not be permitted).
Plan policy 5.1.5 reads “Restrict new development in snow avalanche hazard areas”.
The plan says major recreational assets such as the ski hills will be largely privately managed and operated.
The plan has a policy to consider reliable, accessible public transit as the community grows, which is a future consideration, not an existing service.
I found no ALR land identified in the plan area, which is a provincial Controlled Recreation Area.
BC Transit’s Central Fraser Valley route list (Mission, Abbotsford and Chilliwack routes, plus 66 Fraser Valley Express, 71 Agassiz-Harrison and 72 Hope) has no route to Hemlock Valley.
For a specific lot, send me the address and I’ll look up the zone and the plan designation.

blocks.text: Before you buy in Hemlock Valley

parts.t: Check who sets the zoning.
This area is in the Fraser Valley Regional District, not the City of Mission. Ask the FVRD planning department what the zone and the plan designation allow at the exact address.
Check the avalanche zone.
Ask the FVRD whether the address is in the White, Blue or Red zone and whether a development permit is needed.
Check road access in winter.
Ask who maintains Hemlock Valley Road and what the access is like in snow.
Check the water, sewer and fire protection.
Ask what services the address has and what the nearest emergency service is.
Confirm the school catchment.
Ask School District 75 for the exact address; schools are far away.
For a strata home, read the documents.
The depreciation report, meeting minutes, bylaws and fees, plus any special levies.
Get a full home inspection.
Check the roof, drainage, heating, plumbing and wiring.
